awd_titl_txt: Conference: Student and Early Career Researcher Travel Grant for the 19th Neurosymbolic Learning and Reasoning Conference (NeSy 2025)
awd_abstract_narration:
Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence is broadly understood as the combination of artificial neural network based machine learning (including Large Language Models and more generally deep learning) with symbolic methods from Knowledge Representation and Reasoning. Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence is currently gaining significant interest in academia and industry as a way to further advance AI research and practice related to both fundamental methods and applications in a multitude of fields. This project will provide funds to subsidize the travel expenses of 10 students and early career researchers at U.S. universities to attend the 2025 NeSy conference, held September 8-10 in Santa Cruz, California.

Neurosymbolic Learning and Reasoning (NeSy) is a long-standing meeting (a conference since 2024, previously a workshop), established in 2005, focused on the synergy between neural network methods and symbolic approaches. Covered topics include Neurosymbolic methods for: generative models, knowledge graphs, knowledge representation and reasoning using neural networks, cognitive modeling, probabilistic programming, causal reasoning, and applications. The location of the conference in Santa Cruz, California, which is in close proximity to Silicon Valley, will bring together both academic and industry professionals interested in Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence. This provides a unique opportunity for student and early career researcher networking opportunities across academia and industry. In addition to invited and contributed talks, students will benefit from a doctoral consortium and mentoring activities.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This award supported student and early-career researcher participation in the 19th Neurosymbolic Learning and Reasoning Conference (NeSy 2025), held September 8-10, 2025 at the University of California, Santa Cruz. NeSy brings together researchers working at the intersection of machine learning and symbolic reasoning, including work that combines neural networks and large language models with logic, knowledge representation, and other structured reasoning methods.

The main goal of this award was to make it easier for students and early-career researchers to participate in the NeSy research community. The conference included technical talks, poster presentations, and opportunities for discussion across a broad range of topics in neurosymbolic AI, including trustworthy and interpretable AI, reasoning with large language models, knowledge representation, reinforcement learning, computer vision, and applications of neurosymbolic methods.

The travel support allowed students and early-career researchers to attend the conference in person, present and discuss their work, learn about current research, and meet other researchers working in the area. These in-person interactions are especially important for researchers early in their careers because they provide opportunities to find mentors and collaborators, get feedback on research, and become part of a broader research community.

We were also able to support more attendees than originally planned. The proposal anticipated supporting approximately 10 participants. Instead, we awarded travel support to 19 students and early-career researchers. Eleven attendees received awards of $1,000, and eight attendees received awards of $500. This allowed us to distribute the available funding across a larger group of participants with different levels of travel need.

A major broader impact of the project was reducing financial barriers to conference participation. Students and early-career researchers often have limited travel funding, even when attending a conference is important for presenting their work and building professional connections. This award helped make participation in NeSy 2025 possible for a larger group of emerging researchers and supported continued growth of the U.S. neurosymbolic AI community.

Five travel-grant recipients did not ultimately submit reimbursement requests. As a result, $2,855.45 remained unspent at the end of the award.

Overall, the award supported both the technical goals of NeSy 2025 and the development of its research community. It enabled emerging researchers to participate directly in scientific discussions, share their work, and build connections across the growing field of neurosymbolic AI.
